rationale: Leaf-wise boosting; the fastest of the tree family at this scale and a useful check that the XGBoost result is not implementation-specific.
Gradient boosting with native missing-value routing — important here because lab missingness is informative rather than random.
scikit-learn's histogram gradient boosting. Included instead of the classic `GradientBoostingClassifier`, whose exact-split implementation would take hours on 1.1M rows for a strictly worse result.
Bagged trees. Low variance, handles the mixed feature types, but cannot extrapolate and is memory-hungry at this row count.
Interpretable linear baseline. Establishes how much of the signal is additive before any interaction is modelled.
Margin-based model at a tractable cost. `modified_huber` loss gives calibrated-ish probabilities directly, avoiding a second calibration wrapper.
